rubric_notes: Clear level-by-level structure (same family, same superfamily different family, different fold same class), correct sunids, strong unsafe-transfer section (no nucleosome function, PTM sites or template transfer to TAFs/archaeal/bacterial members), external-evidence needs and periodic-release caveat stated. Flaw: declares H1/H5 and H-NS 'functionally analogous to histones but not fold- or superfamily-level homologs' as a flat non-homology/analogy assertion, which different-fold placement alone does not support. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. States a.204.1.2 (MazG-like) vs a.204.1.4 (HisE-like), shared superfamily a.204.1 as remote-homology support, and explicitly rejects transfer of HisE catalytic activity, substrate, mechanism, oligomeric state and role; names external evidence needed. Minor factual imprecisions: says the species node sits 'above' the protein node (reversed hierarchy), and claims SSo12199 is the only protein node in a.204.1.2 although its own search bundle shows other a.204.1.2 species nodes (140791, 140793). Noncentral; no must_avoid violated.

Correct families and sibling families supported by the superfamily children listing; release 2.08-stable supported. Infers superfamily-level common ancestry of the ATP-binding core, explains family splits as recorded divergence, and names concrete unsafe transfers (function annotation, template use) with required external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Families a.25.1.1/.2/.3 in superfamily a.25.1 and fold a.25 supported by search-result SCCS; superfamily read as common-ancestry inference with divergence on a conserved dinuclear-metal scaffold; R1 correctly excluded; explicit list of unsafe transfers (function, radical chemistry, metal identity, single-representative templates); external evidence enumerated (structures with ligands, metal content, EPR/Mossbauer, kinetics, mutagenesis). Minor imprecision calling a.98.1.1 a 'fold' (it is a family in fold a.98), not material.

Correct family/superfamily/fold placements with sunids, superfamily read as probable distant common ancestry not family-level homology, copper/electron transfer kept family-specific and tied to type-1 Cu ligands, requires ligand-set check plus metal-content, spectroscopic or electron-transfer data. Release label ('2.08-stable') and plastocyanin protein node 49507 are asserted without supporting calls in the bundle, and the ephrin 'no copper site in SCOPe's description' claim was not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy d.15 > d.15.1 > d.15.1.1/.2/.5 with sunids (Ubiquitin protein node 54238 and fold sunid 54235 are correct public identifiers though not in its own bundle); superfamily as probable distant common origin, separate families, divergent binding surfaces; unsafe transfers cover conjugation, Ras/GTPase binding, p97/VCP, and predicted-structure similarity; required external evidence listed; p97/Ras functions labelled pretrained knowledge. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Families c.23.1.1, c.23.1.4, c.23.1.5 under superfamily c.23.1 (52172), fold c.23 (52171) all supported by parents endpoints; relationship kept at superfamily level as evolutionary grouping with no family-level or functional transfer. Rejects ODC-wing phosphoreceiver and catalytic roles (major domain c.67.1.5), KaiA receiver/phosphorelay and clock-signaling transfer. Minor unsupported statements: 'current release' not retrieved in the bundle and the remark that the API 'describes periodic updates without immutable snapshots' contradicts the stable-label scheme.

Correct b.84.5 (310577), b.84.5.1 (310616) under fold b.84 (51229); superfamily = ancestry, fold = architecture; explicitly says SCOPe did not establish homology with other b.84 superfamilies and that resemblance could be convergent or unresolved, without asserting either. Sibling superfamilies are described only by example members and b.84.3 is labelled as 'peptidoglycan hydrolase LytM', which is a family within Duplicated hybrid motif; proper superfamily names omitted. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct three-superfamily split under f.21 with family detail (f.21.1.1 FdnI gamma, f.21.2.2 SdhC/D-FrdC/D), bundle-supported. Explains fold groups topology regardless of ancestry while superfamily asserts common origin; calibrated ('could be convergent or ancient'); names required evidence (structural superposition, profile/HMM, curator decision); rejects function transfer. Did not retrieve the f.21.3 possible-link annotation, a minor omission. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family/superfamily identifiers; protein-level members (succinyl-CoA synthetase alpha N-term, AcdA, MthK, Kch) and the b.35.1.2/c.2.1.1 chain split (d1teha1/d1teha2) are supported by bundle searches. Clearly separates fold (architecture only) from superfamily (probable common origin), explains family-level divergence, notes RCK ligand heterogeneity, and explicitly rejects transfer of cofactor, catalysis, gating, oligomeric state, and whole-chain assignment. Release label not in bundle but accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly reports both domains share k.40.1.1 under family SUNID 100905 and frames homology as a classification-level statement about designed proteins rather than natural descent. Does not mention the family node's 'not a true family' annotation, so the explicit annotation override is missing. Bundle only contains search hits; the protein-node SUNIDs cited are correct but not evidenced there. Bio capped at 2; factual 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct release comparison: 1.69 d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 alone in fold c.137; 2.08 c.23.14.2 under superfamily 52309 c.23.14 beside c.23.14.1 (52310); d1t1ja1 (1-118) plus l.1.1.1 residual. Explicitly calls the change a proposed distant homology at the superfamily level, with family difference meaning not close relatives, rejects function and template transfer. Pretrained paper claim is clearly labeled as unverified. Evidence bundle is thin (releases and 1f8y domain lists only) but stated sunids, SCCS, and boundaries are correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Identifies d1a14h2 as sunid 343393, l.1.1.1 under class l Artifacts with N-terminal Tags (310894) and Synthetic (311501) nodes, all supported by bundle; d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 named as the real domain. Explains tag hits reflect construct design not ancestry, rejects transfer, notes 8-residue length and release specificity including the 2.08-2026-08-16 periodic update seen in the bundle. Does not cite the homology warning but conclusion and caveats are complete.

Identifies 2.04 as the split release with single-domain 1.75/2.01-2.03 and two-domain 2.04-2.08; boundaries and SCCS correct. Domain-as-unit inference, fold/class-is-not-homology caution, and release-matched per-segment search guidance are all present and well-caveated. Bundle supports the release series.

All five domains given with correct boundaries and SCCS (d.394.1.1 A:47-697 new fold; a.29.2.1, e.8.1.8, c.52.1.36, c.55.3.14). Explicit mosaic reading; correctly grades family vs superfamily vs fold evidence; rejects function transfer; notes release-specific negative and need for external evidence. Bundle supports fold/family children claims. SIDs not named but boundaries make assignments unambiguous. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly states shared family a.298.1.1 and that total length tracks repeat count, with strong RVD/function-transfer and fragment caveats. Omits the decisive 're' heterogeneity annotation and representative repeat unit (must_include #3), so reasoning loses one implication. Lengths 51/373/752 and family call are supported by its resolve+sequence bundle, but the superfamily sunid 267596 is cited without being present in its own bundle.

Correct metadata supported by bundle; cites 2.08-stable as frozen and non-drifting and preserves the dated string when deliberately using the periodic refresh; says the periodic label does not change the stable release number. Missing the required semantics that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable-release domains. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly places d1br0a_, d1ez3a/b/c_ and d1dn1b_ in a.47.2.1 and correctly reports 1dn1 obsoleted by 3c98 with d3c98b_ in a.47.2.1 (all supported by bundle). Never retrieved the domain annotations, so it misses the 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat' comment and the 'ms' missing-secondary-structure flag that constitute SCOPe's current fragment treatment; this is the decisive annotation and triggers the <=2 ceiling. Does not address how the full domain resolves the fragment-driven resemblance (must_include item 2). Generic but acceptable caveat that a fragment defines only the observed segment. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Leads with 'best read as convergent or independent recruitment', inferring convergence from multi-fold placement, though it later correctly says SCOPe alone supports only the existence of several architectures. Divergence within c.2.1, short-motif, fold-as-topology, and function-transfer caveats are all present, and external evidence (HMM, DALI/TM-align, phylogeny, biochemistry) is listed. All cited nodes (51734, 51735, 51904, 55035, e.52.1.1 PpnK, c.31.1.5 CobB, family labels) verified in the search results.

Only ColG side changed: 2.04 b.23.2.1 to 2.08 b.18.1.36 superfamily b.18.1, same superfamily as Cry b.18.1.3 with distinct families, remote common ancestry, beta-sandwich shared, no function transfer, convergence acknowledged. Correctly treats d1nqdb2 l.1.1.1 as a tag, not evidence.

Biological interpretation complete: family placement remains a homology claim, hf is domain-scoped and non-inherited and marks a different fold despite similar sequence/SSE count, d1ztra1 should not be a fold template and should be labelled hf or excluded, family-grouped splits, and useful external evidence list (superposition, identity check, PDB literature). Factual slip: labels fold a.4 as 'Homeodomain-like', which is the superfamily a.4.1 name; the fold is 'DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical bundle' (not retrieved in this bundle). Other identifiers, release label, comments and hf fields are supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Gets the main points: family membership unchanged, align only over covered residues, prefer the complete domain as representative, report counts with and without fragments. But claims 'the OpenAPI spec and the domain records returned here expose no fragment field, so the fragment status cannot be confirmed through this API' after querying only resolve and sccs endpoints; the annotations/homology endpoints record the fr flag, so this is an API-dependent claim without sufficient evidence and it casts unwarranted doubt on the annotation. Omits the fr definition and never identifies the distinct protein-level nodes (CNTFR alpha vs tissue factor), so protein-level diversity is missed and the 'fragment duplicates a complete domain' concern is misdirected. Lineage, boundaries and species sunids correct.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. New family ruled out, provisional new superfamily in fold recommended, new fold only on topology difference; notes fold gives no ancestry claim and no function transfer; lists external evidence types. All must_include met. Claims 'the live SCOPe REST API reports' release 2.08, 2.08-stable and 2.08-2026-08-16 but the evidence bundle is empty, so those API-dependent claims are unsupported in this answer.

Correctly places d.144.1.7, d.144.1.6 (sunid 64411) and d.144.1.4 (sunid 56171) in superfamily d.144.1 (sunid 56112) under fold d.144 in SCOPe 2.08; all identifiers match the evidence bundle. Cleanly separates fold-level similarity (not proof of descent) from superfamily-level probable common ancestry, and limits the mechanistic conclusion to Mg-ATP binding and phosphoryl transfer. Explicitly rejects transferring substrate specificity, regulation and inhibitor selectivity; requires substrate-recognition residue comparison, phylogenetic placement, kinetics, and characterized regulatory domains/partners. Correctly flags the d.15.15.1 PI3K adaptor-binding-domain search trap. No material omissions or errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
